memories.memory_text: I told Harper Thorne that when the smoke clears, I'm gonna roll in, hit the bank, take the money, and grab any other fancy shit I can get my hands on.

grounded_facts: Harper Thorne counters Valerie Keller's plan by stating that there will be no valuables left and that money burns.
memories.memory_text: Harper Thorne told me there won't be any fancy shit left and that money burns, like that’s supposed to stop me.

memories.memory_text: I saw the clock on the control panel reach midnight, marking the end of the countdown.

grounded_facts: Valerie Keller pushes the button on the control panel at midnight.
memories.memory_text: I pushed the button on the control panel at midnight.

grounded_facts: Valerie Keller attempts to activate a device multiple times without success, leading to frustration.
memories.memory_text: I kept pressing the button, trying to get the device to activate, but nothing happened no matter how many times I tried.

grounded_facts: Valerie Keller notices the 'Game Boy' in Harper Thorne's hand and blames Harper Thorne for the device malfunction.
memories.memory_text: I saw Harper Thorne holding that Game Boy and immediately thought it was causing the malfunction, so I accused them on the spot.

grounded_facts: Valerie Keller directly blames Harper Thorne for the device failure, attributing it to the 'Game Boy'.
memories.memory_text: I blamed Harper Thorne for the device failing, yelling at them that their Game Boy was interfering.

grounded_facts: Harper Thorne presses another button on the 'Game Boy', potentially triggering an external effect.
memories.memory_text: I saw Harper Thorne press another button on that 'Game Boy' thing, and I wondered if it was causing some kind of effect outside.

grounded_facts: Valerie Keller physically restrains Harper Thorne and demands he fix something, showing urgency and aggression.
memories.memory_text: I charged at Harper Thorne, grabbed him by the throat, and demanded he fix it—I needed him to act right then.

grounded_facts: Harper Thorne throws the Game Boy out of the hatch to prevent Valerie Keller from using it.
memories.memory_text: I saw Harper Thorne throw the Game Boy out the hatch, and I reached after it—I realized he was keeping it from me.

grounded_facts: Cameron Langley opens the old photograph with a machine gun at Valerie Keller, who is standing at the hatch of the brass letter.
memories.memory_text: I was standing at the hatch of the brass letter when I saw Cameron Langley open the old photograph with his machine gun.

grounded_facts: Harper Thorne pushes Valerie Keller out of the way of Cameron Langley's gunfire, saving his life.
Harper Thorne is shot in the shoulder during the attack and falls from the hatch onto the pavement.
memories.memory_text: I felt Harper Thorne push me out of the way just in time, and then I saw him fall from the hatch, wounded in the shoulder.

grounded_facts: Valerie Keller verbally declares his long-standing hatred for Harper Thorne as he lies injured.
memories.memory_text: I told Harper Thorne I hate him, that there's something about him I've always hated, while lying there injured.

grounded_facts: Harper Thorne smiles and reciprocates Valerie Keller's hatred, rejecting any reconciliation or alliance.
memories.memory_text: I saw Harper Thorne smile and say 'Same here,' making it clear he hates me just as much and won't ever reconcile.

grounded_facts: Valerie Keller laughs and claims he didn't need to blow up Harborview Plaza because someone else did it for him.
memories.memory_text: I sat up and laughed, shouting that I didn't have to blow the place up because somebody else did it for me.

grounded_facts: Harper Thorne observes a distant the old photograph rising from Harborview Plaza across Harborview Station, indicating the stenches have crossed over.
memories.memory_text: I realized the stenches must have crossed Harborview Station when I saw the distant the old photograph rising from Harborview Plaza and heard Harper Thorne shouting about it.

grounded_facts: After seeing the the old photograph, Harper Thorne decides to go back to Harborview Plaza and issues orders accordingly.
memories.memory_text: I saw the orange glow across Harborview Station, and I heard Harper Thorne say they got across before ordering me taken inside and declaring we were going back to Harborview Plaza.

grounded_facts: Harper Thorne suggests that Valerie Keller and Sage Bennett would be safer joining them in the brass letter.
memories.memory_text: Harper Thorne told me and Sage Bennett that we'd be safer joining them, but I have no intention of reconciling with him or accepting his offer.

grounded_facts: Harper Thorne informs Valerie Keller of the brass box's location and that it contains guns and ammo.
memories.memory_text: I was told the brass box is down the driveway and it has guns and ammo inside, which I intend to take for myself.

grounded_facts: Harper Thorne sustains a neck wound from Valerie Keller's crossbow, causing blood to trickle from under his chin.
memories.memory_text: I shot Harper Thorne with my crossbow and saw blood trickle from under his chin when he closed the hatch.

grounded_facts: Valerie Keller and Sage Bennett attempt to flee on foot to their car but are ambushed by Sidney Wilder.
memories.memory_text: I ran with Sage Bennett toward our car, trying to escape, but we were ambushed by Sidney Wilder and I had to take one down with my crossbow.

grounded_facts: Valerie Keller is bitten on the hand by a Drew Mercer that had sneaked between him and Sage Bennett.
memories.memory_text: I felt the Drew Mercer's teeth sink into my hand after I slapped what I thought was Sage Bennett, but it wasn't him—it was another Drew Mercer that had slipped between us.

grounded_facts: Valerie Keller kills the Drew Mercer that bit him by driving arrows through its face and skull.
memories.memory_text: I was in agony from the bite, and with no time to reload, I grabbed a fistful of arrows from my quiver and drove them through the Drew Mercer's face and skull to kill it.

grounded_facts: Valerie Keller mistakenly slaps a Drew Mercer thinking it is Sage Bennett, triggering an attack.
memories.memory_text: I slapped what I thought was Sage Bennett on the back, but it wasn't him—it was a Drew Mercer that had slipped between us, and it grabbed my hand and bit me.

grounded_facts: Sage Bennett points his rifle at Valerie Keller's forehead, offering him a choice after the bite.
memories.memory_text: I felt the cold aim of Sage Bennett's rifle at my forehead, and when he said 'Your choice,' I knew my fate was in his hands.

grounded_facts: Valerie Keller accepts his likely transformation after being bitten, refusing to be shot by Sage Bennett and instead urging Sage Bennett to escape.
memories.memory_text: I refused to let Sage Bennett shoot me, even after the bite — I laughed it off because I knew I was already changing, and I had to accept that.

grounded_facts: Valerie Keller tells Sage Bennett to take the car and leave, sacrificing himself.
memories.memory_text: I told Sage Bennett to take the car and get out of here, knowing I couldn't make it and wanting him to survive.

grounded_facts: Sage Bennett refuses Valerie Keller's offer to escape alone and insists Valerie Keller take the car instead.
Sage Bennett refuses to leave and tells Valerie Keller to take the car instead.
memories.memory_text: I offered to let Sage Bennett take the car and escape, but he refused and told me to take it instead, saying he'd get out of there.

grounded_facts: Valerie Keller unlocks the steel doors of the depot using a mag-key.
memories.memory_text: I jumped out of the brass box and ran to the steel doors, unlocking them with my mag-key.

grounded_facts: Valerie Keller moves with determination along the deserted subway tracks under Harborview Station.
memories.memory_text: I moved forward with determination along the deserted subway tracks under Harborview Station, focusing on making progress through the dark tunnel.

grounded_facts: Sawyer Sloane shoots three rounds at fleeing security guards, wounding one, escalating internal conflict among survivors.
memories.memory_text: I saw Sawyer Sloane the old photograph three shots at the fleeing guards, and one of them went down wounded.

grounded_facts: Valerie Keller wounds Sawyer Sloane in the calf and shoulder with arrows, slowing his escape and increasing his vulnerability.
memories.memory_text: I shot Sawyer Sloane in the calf and then in the shoulder with my crossbow, slowing him down and making it harder for him to get away.

grounded_facts: After being shot, Sawyer Sloane hurls a racial slur at Valerie Keller, intensifying personal enmity.
memories.memory_text: I heard Sawyer Sloane shout a racial slur at me after I shot him, calling me a 'fucking spic bastard,' which made it clear how much he hated me.

grounded_facts: Valerie Keller suggests talking when Sawyer Sloane is 'less excited,' implying a twisted respect or unresolved history.
memories.memory_text: I told Sawyer Sloane that we should talk when he's less excited, because he was clearly too angry and in pain to think straight.

grounded_facts: Valerie Keller confronts Sawyer Sloane, declaring he wants him to die the same death he will suffer after being bitten.
memories.memory_text: I confronted Sawyer Sloane and told him I don't care about anything anymore, that I'm going to get him, and he should talk to me when he's less excited—because I want him to die the same way I will after being bitten.

grounded_facts: A chaotic confrontation in the Pinecrest House as survivors attempt to hold off Sidney Wilder breaching the building's main entrance.
memories.memory_text: I was in the Pinecrest House when the Sidney Wilder started pounding on the glass doors, and everything turned chaotic—Sawyer Sloane shot at the guards, then aimed at me, so I shot him back with my crossbow while Elliot Warren broke through the doors.

grounded_facts: After being shot, Elliot Warren locks onto Sawyer Sloane as his primary target, showing unusual focus.
memories.memory_text: After Sawyer Sloane shot him, I saw Elliot Warren lock onto Sawyer Sloane with a focused intensity that felt unnatural, like he wasn't just another Drew Mercer anymore.

grounded_facts: Elliot Warren leads the Sidney Wilder into the Pinecrest House after breaching the doors, becoming the primary physical threat.
memories.memory_text: I saw Elliot Warren break through the doors with his hammer and lead the Sidney Wilder into the Pinecrest House, becoming the main threat right away.

grounded_facts: Sawyer Sloane kicks the nozzle out and is drenched in gasoline while trying to escape.
memories.memory_text: I saw Sawyer Sloane kick the nozzle out and get soaked with gasoline while trying to escape.

grounded_facts: The reanimated Valerie Keller confronts and slams Sawyer Sloane onto the car hood, preparing to feed.
memories.memory_text: I reached for Sawyer Sloane, vengeance in my eyes, and slammed him down across the hood, ready to feed.

grounded_facts: Elliot Warren rolls an oil pot down the ramp, igniting a fireball that incinerates Sawyer Sloane and Valerie Keller.
memories.memory_text: I reached for Sawyer Sloane, ready to make him pay, and slammed him down across the hood, but then I saw the fireball coming and couldn't escape—it consumed me and him in an instant.

grounded_facts: Sawyer Sloane removes arrow shanks from his leg and shoulder, indicating he was recently wounded.
memories.memory_text: I saw Sawyer Sloane snap off the arrow shanks in his leg and shoulder, and I reached for him, ready to take my vengeance, but then the fireball engulfed us both.

grounded_facts: Harper Thorne initially sees a terrifying figure approaching but relaxes upon recognizing it as Remy Finch, a familiar but disfigured guerrilla fighter.
memories.memory_text: I saw Harper Thorne turn and look at me, and I noticed how he relaxed once he recognized me, even though I know I look terrifying with my burned face.

grounded_facts: Remy Finch initiates a conversation with Harper Thorne, asking what he's doing, establishing familiarity despite his disturbing appearance.
memories.memory_text: I saw Harper Thorne and called out to him, asking what he was doing, like we always did—familiar, despite how I must look.

memories.memory_text: Harper Thorne told me the town is full of Sidney Wilder, acting like regular people, which sounded like a new kind of trouble.

grounded_facts: A group of armed survivors, including Harper Thorne, Sidney Davenport, Remy Finch, and Evan Colter, are present in a fortified interior space at night, preparing and communicating during a crisis.
memories.memory_text: I remember being in the fortified space at night with Harper Thorne, Sidney Davenport, and Evan Colter, where we were arming ourselves and getting ready as the situation unfolded around us.

grounded_facts: Mortar tubes on the brass letter launch fireworks into the sky, intended to distract stenches.
memories.memory_text: I looked up at the fireworks launching from the mortar tubes on the brass letter and called them 'sky flowers' because they weren't the kind you put on graves—they were way up in Heaven.

grounded_facts: Harper Thorne expresses affection for Remy Finch, citing his belief in heaven as a redeeming quality.
memories.memory_text: I remember Harper Thorne telling me, 'I love ya, Remy Finch. Know why? Cuzz you still believe in heaven,' and it made me feel valued for who I am.

grounded_facts: Valerie Keller calls Remy Finch an idiot, but Remy Finch counters by implying his armed readiness and intelligence.
memories.memory_text: When Valerie Keller called me an idiot, I stood my ground and reminded him I'm always ready—he can see the iron on me, and I know he sees more than just a fool.

memories.memory_text: I saw the zombie emerge from the smoke and attack Wesley Hart, confirming we were facing an immediate threat.

memories.memory_text: I heard the wood groan, saw that skull move—just a Avery Sloane twitching—and I put an arrow through its head before it could do anything else. One shot, clean through the skull.
I jumped out of the van with the three guerrillas, looked at Harper Thorne, and asked, 'Ready?'—then fired up my bike and took off, yelling 'YEEEE-HAAAAAAAA!'
I shot Harper Thorne a sarcastic line about not having any fun after he gave me that irritated look—like he’s got the right to judge how we run things.
I told Sidney Davenport to come with me and showed him the ropes by having him hop on the back of my bike—we’re heading out for supplies, and now he’s learning how things really work.

I didn’t wait for Harper Thorne to finish talking—I just walked into the liquor store with Sage Bennett. The doors were wide open, and all I saw was darkness ahead, but that didn’t matter. Fifteen hundred a jug, and he wanted to walk away?

I had both hands on the case of Dom Perignon when a third hand grabbed it—some Avery Sloane with a swastika on its forehead lunging out of the dark. I punched it in the face while it tried to bite me, and for a second, I felt the weight of it crushing down on me.
I saw a dead cop grab Sidney Davenport's ankle and bite his leg. I shot it in the head with my crossbow. Then Sidney Davenport put his gun under his chin and killed himself.
I told Harper Thorne that we all know the risks when we take the job — Sidney Davenport got bit, same as I would’ve, and his number came up. That’s just how it is.
I looked at that screen showing Pinecrest House and told Harper Thorne I’m done following paths like my old man — I’ve got the money now, and I’m buying my way into my own place.
I handed over my guns at the checkpoint, just like they wanted. Got a claim check back—same as everyone else going in clean.
I heard a scream down the corridor—sharp, panicked—so I dropped the champagne and Cohibas and started running.
The door to Penthouse Two was locked, and another scream came from inside—I threw myself at it, felt the latch splinter, and busted it open.

I brought Sawyer Sloane champagne and cigars. I poured champagne into a highball glass and gave it to him, then lit two cigars—one for me and one for him. I told him I had enough money to buy a place in the Green. He said there was a long waiting list and that membership needed board approval.

I grabbed Sawyer Sloane by the collar after he denied me, screamed that I'd cleaned up his garbage for three years and knew what was in it—he pressed a .45 into my side, still smiling, and called the guards to drag me out.
I spun fast, slugged one guard straight in the jaw, and felt his head snap back before I moved to the next.
After dropping the third guard with a kick to the face, I bolted through the the old photograph door—metal slamming behind me as I hit the street.
I woke Sage Bennett up in that run-down bedroom and told him we're taking the truck out — time to move. When he asked about Harper Thorne, I shut it down. Not him. Just the regular guys.
I flashed the paper and told the guard I was taking the truck out—he hesitated when he saw it was dated yesterday, and I knew I had one second to decide whether to pull the gun or back down.
I stopped my team from jumping into the firefight—Stenches were tearing into the guards, and I saw the opening. Told them, 'Ain't our fight,' then pointed us straight at the truck.
I told Sawyer Sloane I'd blow him out of his ivory tower if he didn't hand over all the money in his bank—I've got the red notebook, and that's what gives me the power.
I told Avery Bennett to call me at midnight from the pier to let me know if we were rich or not—right after he jumped out and ran for the boat shed.
I watched the Blair Arden through the windshield, knowing if I didn't take that shot, I'd be just another disposable body to Sawyer Sloane. I fired the crossbow through the window—clean, one shot.
I checked my watch—11:29—and keyed the transmitter. 'Avery Bennett. Anything?'
I opened the hatch and told Sage Bennett to get out and check the place—gates were open, no one in sight, something felt off. Then I told someone to go help him, and Logan Bellamy moved.
I told them to stop when we had the Johnsons secured—enough was enough. The next move was already clear: we were going to blow up the Green.

I saw Harper Thorne and his guy in the road, told Evan Colter to stop, took the Sidney Davenport and called out—Harper Thorne showed up outta nowhere with that Game Boy tracker, said they wanted in. I said 'Open up,' even though Sage Bennett thought I was crazy.
I asked who else was out there, and when Harper Thorne admitted Sawyer Sloane’s men were dealt with, I confirmed the Johnsons were with us and ordered Evan Colter to set the cannons.
Harper Thorne told me not to do it, but I told him straight—Sawyer Sloane's got it coming. I wasn't gonna back down, not after everything.
I remember telling them — he killed our friends, and every week we were the ones dumping bodies for Sawyer Sloane, doing his dirty work until he threw me away like trash.

memories.memory_text: I asked the kid if we're all just pretending to be alive—because sometimes it feels like surviving isn't the same as living.

I turned and saw Remy Finch step out of the shadows—half his face burned off, one eye bulging—and for a second, I braced for a fight, but then I recognized him. He was still sharp, still talking, and that’s when it hit me: if he could adapt, so could the Sidney Wilder.

I handed Graham Brooks a beer, and the next second he was on me—snarling, clawing—no warning, just pure animal. I smashed the bottle on the red notebook and drove the glass into his skull before he choked the life out of me.
I grabbed Valerie Keller by the shirt and slammed him against the wall. Two people were dead, and Sidney Davenport shouldn't have died for liquor and cigars.
I looked at that monitor showing rich people in their club, and I knew—places like Pinecrest House were never meant for us. We're the wrong kind.
I told Logan Winslow 'Everyone's stoppable'—he was drunk on revolution, standing there with his whiskey, thinking numbers could bring down the Green. I knew better. No army fixes this place.
I saw the boy coughing behind Logan Winslow—pale, feverish—and I gave him the antibiotics. Didn't say much. Just pressed the bottle into Logan Winslow's hand and kept moving.

I ripped off part of my shirt to bandage Wesley Hart's arm. I asked him why he was thrown into the arena. When he started telling me his story, I told him I didn't want to hear it—everybody's got a story, and I'm tired of hearing them.

I told Wesley Hart I was going north to Canada—somewhere with no people. Then we saw Logan Winslow being chased and beaten by security men through the alley; I reached through the bars, but I couldn't do a damn thing.

The cell door clanged open and the guard demanded, 'Which one of you is Harper Thorne?'—I froze for half a second, eyes locking with Remy Finch and Wesley Hart, knowing that name wasn't mine, but now it was a noose around my neck.
I led the team into the depot, M-16 up, scanning the smoke—bodies torn apart, fences pushed in from outside. These stenches are learning, working together like in Uniontown.
After Remy Finch's shot, the growling in the smoke had everyone spooked—I grabbed the Motorola and keyed the radio. 'Harper Thorne. Calling the Green.'

I pointed my gun at Sidney Nolan and Cameron Langley, told them I was taking the red notebook and going to Canada—no discussion, no hesitation. If they didn’t like it, the Sidney Wilder in the marsh were their other option.

I held up the Game Boy unit, the red dot blinking on the screen—my homing device still working, tracking the red notebook. Wesley Hart asked how I knew where to go, and I showed her: I built the damn thing to find it.
I told the team to stay put and watch the hatches—the red notebook’s got steel skin too thick to shoot through, so I’m going in alone, hoping words get me inside.
I pressed another button on the Game Boy just as Valerie Keller turned on me, his voice roaring over the silence that followed his failed attempt to start the system.
I told Valerie Keller 'Not a chance,' and threw the device out the hatch—he lunged for it, but it was already gone.
I saw the gun barrel flash out of the corner of my eye—no time to shout, just push Valerie Keller down and take the hit myself. The bullet tore into my shoulder as I hit the pavement.
I held Spencer Keller and Logan Bellamy at gunpoint while checking the clock—12:01—and keyed the transmitter to call the Green, my voice steady despite the chaos behind me.
I told him I was taking his fucking truck — no hesitation, just the way it had to be.

I saw the orange glow across Harborview Station and moved between the houses on the hillside to get a clear view—Harborview Plaza was on the old photograph. The stenches had crossed Harborview Station. They actually got across the fucking Harborview Station.
I told them to take the brass box—guns and ammo inside—and said they'd be safer coming with us. Valerie Keller refused, but I made sure they had a chance.
Wesley Hart tore off her bandana and used it to wipe the blood from my neck—her hands steady, her eyes sharp. I didn’t flinch, but I felt it, that quiet moment where she almost lost me.

I traced my finger along the monitor, mapping the route above the Throat—no bridges, no warzone. We come in high, avoid the fighting, and open a way out. That fence wasn’t just a barrier. It was a cage.
I sprinted up the tilting roadbed and jumped the widening gap just before the bridge dropped too far, landing hard and rolling as I hit the other side.
I ran out from the tree line and saw the Throat—people screaming, getting torn apart, the fence sparking as bodies hit it. The air was thick with smoke and the smell of burning flesh.
A Avery Sloane lunged at me—three feet away—so I shot it in the head. Blood sprayed, lit up by the headlights of the red notebook just before it crushed the body. Then I stepped into its path.
I didn't flinch as the vehicle bore down on me—then everything went black. Next thing I know, I'm clawing my way up the windshield, hands scraping against glass, Remy Finch screaming my name.
I leapt off the gun the second before the charge blew—felt the heat of the explosion on my back as I hit the ground running, the first through the breach.
I was firing blind into the dark, dropping Sidney Wilder as they grabbed people—saved a woman with a baby, a couple, a priest—until the gun clicked empty and the horde started closing in.
I saw Shawn Sterling's face covered in blood after they mowed down Avery Sloane things, and when Logan Winslow asked me to rejoin, I just shook my head and told him it was all his.
I lowered the binoculars and said it out loud—'All they want is somewhere to go. Same as us.' It hit me then, clear and quiet, that we weren't so different.
I looked at Wesley Hart, then told Evan Colter to take us North—no hesitation, just the order, and they followed.

memories.memory_text: I reached out and touched the paint on Dead Black’s face, then looked at my fingers—now stained red.
They threw me in that cage like meat, and I knew—right then—I had to move, had to fight, had to stay alive even if they already called me Dead Red.

I told Harper Thorne the truth about why I was in the arena—it wasn't the little man, it was the one upstairs. I told him I was working with Logan Winslow, trying to push back against the system that keeps us all down, chewing on bones while they eat steak.

I asked Harper Thorne to take me when he escapes—wherever he’s going. I told him I can shoot and be useful, that I had Army training before they decided I was better off as a hooker. I needed him to see I wasn’t just dead weight.
The cell door clanged open and a guard asked for Harper Thorne—I didn't move, but my pulse jumped. Harper Thorne, Remy Finch, and I all looked at each other, silent, wondering what this meant now.
I said I'd take the gun, and when the soldier asked if I could handle it, I told him I could—better than him, and pointed out the safety was off. He had to click it on before handing it over.
I tied my hair back, checked my clip, and said I'd feel like a dick if I didn't go—Harper Thorne was asking if we wanted in, and I knew I had to move, even if I didn't give a damn about the place.

I saw the stenches had torn through the fence, and beyond that—suburb, Harborview Station, the Pinecrest House tower glowing in the distance. That's when it hit me: they're not just wandering. They want Harborview Plaza.

Remy Finch wet the sight of his rifle with his thumb, whispering it catches the moonlight so he can aim. I didn't get why he'd do something like that—seemed strange, ritualistic—so I asked him, quiet, 'Why do you do that?'
Remy Finch's shot barely missed me, but it took out the Drew Mercer behind me—bullet buzzed my ear and blew a wisp of hair. I felt the heat of it, heard the crack, then saw Avery Sloane man drop.
I shot the bridal Drew Mercer just as it went for Remy Finch—my bullet clipped his ear, but dropped Graham Brooks in time. He yelled it hurt, but I called it even.

I was driving, and Harper Thorne told me to pull over out of nowhere—then he pointed his gun at Sidney Nolan and Cameron Langley, laid it out plain: he wasn't saving the Green for anyone, he was taking the car and going to Canada. When I realized he'd been planning this all along, I said, 'No. I like the way you think,' because that’s what you do when someone shows they’re not playing the sucker.

I was driving the Impala down the country road at night when Harper Thorne suddenly said the red notebook was heading to Ross Park. He said it's the powder magazine—where they keep the rockets for the cannons.

I yanked the brass box into the driveway hard, tires crunching gravel, and killed the engine under Harper Thorne’s shout—just in time to see Harborview Plaza lights sprawl below, knowing they’d be coming up that road soon.
I asked Harper Thorne if he was really going out there alone—told him he’d need our guns, but he said the red notebook’s got steel skin an inch thick and you can’t shoot your way in.
I saw the hatch open from the shadows—we were close enough to see it, but not close enough to stop it. That’s when I knew waiting was over.
I aimed my K-90 at Valerie Keller through the rustling branches, voice steady—'That man pulls the trigger, he's dead.'
I remember the guns on the vehicle starting to turn toward Harborview Plaza with this loud whirring sound — I knew we didn’t have much time left.
I shot Cameron Langley in the head while the Drew Mercer was tearing into him—no hesitation. He had the gun on Valerie Keller, and the moment was gone if I waited.

After the shot, I opened the old photograph on the Drew Mercer with Sidney Nolan—the two of us laying down the old photograph until it was destroyed. I could see Graham Brooks bucking and sparking, then going still.
I saw the orange glow across Harborview Station and told Harper Thorne to look—the old photograph was rising from Harborview Plaza, and I knew the stenches had gotten through.
I pulled off my bandana to wipe the blood from Harper Thorne’s neck. He looked at me like it meant something—I almost lost him.
I said we could blast our way through the barricades. It was a direct option—clear the path fast.
I jumped out right after Harper Thorne, and when she fired, I knew I had to do more than just follow—I had to act. Saying 'Making myself useful' wasn't just words; it was me stepping into it.
I saw the rat—half its body gone, ass blown off—but still skittering forward. Remy Finch didn't hit the head, and that's when I knew: same as the people, only a headshot stops them.
They came at me from the road—skreeing, swarming—so I vaulted the railing and dropped to the riverbank. But they were already down there too, crawling everywhere.
I felt the rats snap at my hands as I cut the tether—jaws closing on air just past my fingers—but I kept sawing at the rope with the jackknife until it frayed and gave.
Once the current took the dinghy, I was crouched on the upturned hull, adrift with no paddles and no way to steer—just Harborview Station pulling me into the dark.
I reached out with my hand and it hit something long and slimy—thought it was a snake, but it wasn't. It was a rope, thick with moss, and I grabbed it hard, starting to pull.
I was pulling on the rope when a face suddenly bobbed up out of the water—eyes blinking—floating right past me. It was the Bridgekeeper's head. I screamed.
I grabbed Shawn Sterling as he ran past me, panicked—couldn't let him get caught in the open with those things closing in.
I ran with Shawn Sterling past the manhole, flames swirling from the oil pots, workers throwing them like comets at the Sidney Wilder—no time to stop, just move.
I helped pull open the cell doors after the keys turned in the locks, and Logan Winslow and his men came out.

I whispered Harper Thorne's name in the dark, then stepped out from behind one of Avery Sloane things—he turned, and we moved toward each other through the frozen Sidney Wilder, meeting in silence before the guns tore it all apart.
I said we’d take them with us—Remy Finch and Harper Thorne. The others didn’t object, but it was my call to make.
